title: NVIDIA (NVDA): Seven Times Earnings, Priced for a Normal Chip Cycle
description: NVIDIA lost 23% in its worst week since 2008 as Jensen Huang resigned, the 10-Q slipped and the SEC reportedly probed its accounting. At $125.53 it sits on its 200-week line and within 2% of my cycle-aware value, with half its free cash flow going back into its own customers. I wait for the 10-Q.
verdict_label: Wait — fairly priced for a normal chip cycle; buy on a clean 10-Q or under $100
selection_rationale: A market-wide AI sell-off put eight of the ten shortlisted names down 25-34%, mostly on sector beta (quantum, neoclouds, space). NVDA's 23% fall had company-specific causes: the CEO's resignation, a delayed 10-Q and a reported SEC accounting probe, in the world's most widely held stock, now sitting on its 200-week line. The piece answers whether the earnings are real and whether 7.6x forward earnings is cheap or a peak-cycle multiple. Passed on SMMT (single-asset trial readout), GLBE (smaller beat-and-raise sell-off) and the sector-beta names.
